Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
**Exercise 1 — Delete and reschedule.** Add a `delete_event(date, time)` tool to the Calendar Helper. Update the system prompt so the agent knows it can reschedule by deleting and re-adding. Test with "Move my Q3 planning to 3pm tomorrow."

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Add a `@tool` function that filters the `CALENDAR[date]` list to remove entries matching the time. In the prompt, mention: "To reschedule, call delete_event then add_event." Keep the tools composable — don't write a `reschedule_event` tool, let the agent compose.
</details>

**Exercise 2 — Vector search in the KB.** Replace the naive word-count scoring in `DocStore.search` with `sentence-transformers` cosine similarity. Embed each doc once at `__init__`, embed the query on each search, return top-3 by cosine.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

`pip install sentence-transformers`, then in `__init__`: `self.model = SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2'); self.embeddings = self.model.encode([d['body'] for d in self.docs])`. In `search`: `q_emb = self.model.encode([query]); scores = self.embeddings @ q_emb.T`. This sets up Day 13's RAG work.
</details>

**Exercise 3 — Persist the calendar.** Swap the in-memory `CALENDAR` dict for a SQLite file using `sqlite3`. Make sure `add_event` commits and `list_events` reads fresh each call.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Use a module-level `sqlite3.Connection` with `check_same_thread=False`. Schema: `CREATE TABLE events (date TEXT, time TEXT, title TEXT, duration INTEGER)`. Index on `(date, time)`. Don't forget to `conn.commit()` after inserts.
</details>
